cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Tax Machine prepare W-2s, each employee's yearly pay statement, for HANGS Construction Services.
It starts from this year's four payroll returns.
Next, the year's payroll: every employee's earnings, the roster, and the payroll ledger.
It also reads the company vehicle log, since personal use of a company truck counts as pay.
It confirms everyone paid is on the roster.
Now it checks the official W-2 rules online, from wage limits to the box 12 codes.
Then it builds a W-2 for each of the 101 employees.
Box 1 wages come to just under $11.2 million.
It adds the box 12 codes for retirement savings and overtime pay.
It flags personal use of two company pickups, missing from pay.
Now the checks: the W-3 summary matches the four quarterly returns exactly.
The payroll ledger agrees as well.
Thirteen cents of extra Social Security tax gets refunded.
Last, it writes the draft forms and the workpapers behind them.

All done. 101 draft W-2s report just under $11.2 million of wages in box 1. Five items stay open: personal use of two company pickups to add to pay, 13 cents of Social Security tax to refund, a missing Social Security number, a check on overtime, and the filing itself. A person reviews and e-files by February 1; nothing is filed yet.
Here are the results: 101 draft W-2s with just under $11.2 million of wages, and five open items for a person to decide.
